title: Spreadsheet Template Zones
panelPrompt: Click a zone to see which columns belong to it and why.

image.style: flat vector mock-spreadsheet illustration, clean grid lines, muted textbook palette
image.overall: A mock tracking spreadsheet drawn as a clean grid, filling the frame. It has one header row across the top and about five data rows beneath it. The columns are grouped into three visually distinct blocks separated by a slightly heavier vertical divider line: a NARROW left block of two columns, a WIDE centre block of about six columns, and a NARROW right block of one column. Each block's header cells are tinted in that block's accent colour. The ONLY text in the image is the short header words in the header row: in the left block "Name" and "Joined"; in the centre block six short badge names "First Program", "Loops", "Variables", "Functions", "Sensors", "Debugging"; in the right block "Notes".
image.layoutNotes: Draw the three column blocks so their left and right boundaries are unambiguous, with a heavier divider between blocks than between the columns inside a block, so the overlay's rectangular hover zones line up with the block boundaries exactly. The left block should span roughly 3% to 30% of the image width, the centre block roughly 32% to 75%, and the right block roughly 77% to 97%. Fill the data cells with neutral grey placeholder bars and small tick or short date-like dashes -- do NOT write real names, real dates, or any readable content in the data cells. Only the header row carries readable words.

zones.label: Identity columns
facts: The only columns a substitute mentor needs to find a specific student

draw.position: The narrow left block of two columns, roughly 3% to 30% of the image width.
draw.visual: Two columns with blue-tinted header cells reading "Name" and "Joined", with short neutral grey placeholder bars in the cells beneath.

zones.label: Badge columns
zones.summary: What has been mastered, and when.
facts: One column per badge or skill, in the order they are typically earned
Each cell holds a completion date, not just a checkmark
Grouped together so progress is scannable left to right

draw.position: The wide centre block of about six columns, roughly 32% to 75% of the image width.
draw.visual: Six narrow columns with green-tinted header cells carrying the six short badge names, with small date-like dashes in some cells and blanks in others, creating a visible staircase of completion from left to right.

zones.label: Notes column
zones.summary: Anything that does not fit a fixed column.
facts: Free-text field for context a mentor wants the next mentor to see
Kept to short, factual notes -- not a substitute for the parent communication log
Always the rightmost column so it never disrupts the badge block

draw.position: The narrow right block of one wide column, roughly 77% to 97% of the image width.
draw.visual: A single wide column with an amber-tinted header cell reading "Notes", its cells containing longer neutral grey placeholder bars suggesting free text.

quiz.question: Which zone holds a completion date rather than a checkmark?
Which zone is always kept rightmost so it never disrupts the others?
Which zone does a substitute mentor use to find a specific student?
